tldr: HuggingGPT is an LLM-powered agent that uses ChatGPT as a controller to autonomously plan, select, and execute tasks using expert models from Hugging Face, enabling the solution of complex multi-modal AI tasks.
contributions: Proposed HuggingGPT with an inter-model cooperation protocol that applies LLMs as the brain for planning and decision while automatically invoking and executing expert models for specific tasks.

Integrated the Hugging Face hub with numerous task-specific models around ChatGPT to tackle generalized AI tasks covering multiple modalities and domains, providing multimodal and reliable conversation services.
Formulated and evaluated task planning and model selection capabilities of LLMs across different task types (single, sequential, and graph tasks).
Conducted extensive experiments on challenging AI tasks across language, vision, speech, and cross-modality to demonstrate HuggingGPT's capability.
methods: HuggingGPT operates in four stages: (1) Task Planning — ChatGPT analyzes user requests and decomposes them into structured sub-tasks with dependencies using a JSON-format prompt template with demonstrations; (2) Model Selection — ChatGPT selects appropriate models from Hugging Face based on their language descriptions, filtering by task type and ranking by download count to manage context limits; (3) Task Execution — Selected models are invoked with dynamically resolved resource dependencies (using <resource>-task_id symbols), with independent tasks executed in parallel; (4) Response Generation — ChatGPT integrates all inference results and generates human-readable responses.
results: HuggingGPT can tackle a wide range of sophisticated AI tasks spanning different modalities and domains. Experiments were conducted on single tasks (e.g., object detection, image classification), sequential tasks (e.g., pose detection → pose-to-image generation → image-to-text → text-to-speech), and graph tasks (e.g., image similarity retrieval) across language, vision, speech, and cross-modality. Evaluation metrics included Precision, Recall, F1, Accuracy, Edit Distance, and GPT-4 Score for task planning. Specific numerical results are truncated in the provided text.
limitations: Current LLMs are limited to text input/output and lack native ability to process complex information such as vision and speech. For challenging tasks, LLMs are weaker than fine-tuned expert models even in zero-shot/few-shot settings. The approach requires collecting high-quality model descriptions, which may involve prompt engineering. Additionally, context length limits constrain the number of models that can be considered simultaneously, requiring filtering and ranking strategies.
